sheets.prompt:
Revise the LAST reference image into a consistent AR C A N A GUARDIANS base-game character sheet. This is a substantial proportion AND material-style correction, not a mild color adjustment.
REFERENCE HIERARCHY:
1) FIRST reference (the square base game's atlas): the TOP ROW OF FOUR HEROES is the binding reference for head-to-body ratio, faces, limbs, readable weapons, silhouette and stylized painted texture. Make every new character belong in that exact roster.
2) SECOND reference (the tall key art): use only its jewel teal / forest green / ivory / warm bronze palette and polished hand-painted fantasy materials; do not borrow its setting, camera or longer body proportions.
3) LAST reference: preserve its four character identities, cultures, costume color assignments, species and signature weapons, but REBUILD the bodies to match the atlas heroes. The last reference's realistic long bodies and tiny repetitive textures are incorrect.

STRICT PROPORTION: all four adult fantasy heroes about 2.5 to 3 heads tall measured from skull top to sole, excluding hats/horns/weapons. Head occupies roughly 34-38 percent of actual standing body height. Very large expressive heads, short neck or no visible neck, compact torso, thick short forearms and shins, broad hands and boots, chunky shoulders and large readable weapons. Human elves/mages/duelists MUST be equally compact; do not leave them 5-7 heads tall. Retain adult character identity, not literal infant faces. No long slender legs, no fashion-illustration silhouette.
MATERIAL: polished hand-painted, rounded/beveled three-dimensional fantasy game asset look matching the atlas; clean broad color planes, soft warm highlights and darker local shadow grooves. Metal has broad controlled gold/steel highlights, leather broad stitching and 2-3 creases, cloth broad matte folds, wood a few broad grain strokes, fur sculpted in a few clumps, crystal only a few clear facets. Remove photographic pores, grain noise, micro-embroidery, countless buckles, filigree, fine feather hairs and photorealism. Preserve genuine separation between cloth/metal/wood, avoid smooth plastic/vinyl or flat vector. Saturated rich colors, not dusty desaturation. Small quantities of magical glow only. Main material, contrasting cloth, and one small element accent per character.
OUTPUT COMPOSITION: high-quality square concept board, exactly four equally sized panels in a 2 by 2 grid, clean warm pale parchment background, very thin muted gold panel dividers, full body entirely visible including weapon tips and feet, ample blank space. Three-quarter standing hero view with slight view from above like atlas, neutral clear readable stance and small contact shadow. All four at similar visual scale with no scene or environment. Simple labels A upper left, B upper right, C lower left, D lower right; no other text, no titles. Make visually obvious at first glance that these are the same compact game family as the original atlas heroes.

C: boar beastfolk shield warrior, huge friendly tusked head, a chunky wooden round shield with teal tree emblem and an oversized blocky bronze hammer. D: mushroom-folk herbalist, very large red-brown mushroom cap, round glasses, short ivory coat and teal sash, simple carved wooden lantern staff and herb satchel.
